title: Persuading
job: Make a case, concede a point, hold your ground
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: quamquam TAKES THE INDICATIVE AND licet THE SUBJUNCTIVE, AND BOTH MEAN 'ALTHOUGH'. quamquam venit, tamen nōn gaudeō concedes a FACT — he really is coming. licet veniat concedes a possibility, with L3-M4's mood. That is the module's hardest pair and the only guide is this: licet is ALSO a verb, meaning 'it is allowed', so it behaves like one and takes a mood after it. After four modules of subjunctives a learner's reflex is the mood, and quamquam is where the reflex is wrong.

quamquam AND tamen WORK AS A PAIR, and Latin is happier than English about writing both. 'Although … still' feels redundant in English and is the normal shape here — the same asymmetry as M2's ideō … quia. tamen still comes SECOND in its clause, which L3-M3 settled, and it is one of six words in this course that must.

certē … sed IS THE CONCEDE-AND-HOLD FRAME AND IT COSTS ONE WORD. certē is new; sed is L1-M9's. Grant the point, then keep your position — and because the frame is almost free, the module's cap goes on the two concessive conjunctions and the two question particles instead. Three concessive words in one sentence (quamquam, certē, tamen) is normal Latin and heavier in translation than in the original.

nōnne EXPECTS YES AND num EXPECTS NO, AND BOTH KEYS WERE HELD FREE FOR THIRTY-THREE MODULES. L1-M2 taught -ne for a NEUTRAL yes-or-no question and wrote nōnne and num nowhere, so that this module could have the loaded ones. nōnne is nōn plus -ne, which is why 'is he not coming?' is the literal shape and 'surely he is' the meaning. Between them they are the politest tools in the course, because each one tells the listener which answer you are hoping for — which is what makes a question persuasive rather than neutral.

licet TAKES THE MOOD'S PAST FOR A PAST CONCESSION: licet errāverim, 'although I may have been wrong' — the PERFECT subjunctive. M3 opened the pluperfect and imperfect subjunctives for counterfactuals and this is a fourth tense of the same mood, but it costs nothing new to build: the perfect stem plus -erim. A concession about the past needs it, and nothing else in this module does.

sentences.cue: Although he is coming, I am not glad.

words.note: 'Although', and it takes the INDICATIVE — a plain fact conceded. Its partner licet takes a subjunctive and means the same thing.
'He comes' — veniō's third person present, and one bar from vēnit, 'he came'.
'Not', in front of what it denies. L1-M3's word.
'I am glad': gaudeō, gaudet. L4-M3's verb, and here in the plain indicative.

sentences.trap: quamquam takes the plain indicative, which is the opposite of what a learner will expect after a level of subjunctives. It concedes a FACT — he really is coming — and the concession is in the conjunction rather than in a mood.
sentences.sound: QUAM-quam VE-nit, nōn GAU-de-ō. Seven syllables and only quamquam is heavy.

words.note: 'Certainly', and it concedes before it disagrees. certē … sed is the frame: grant the point, then hold your ground.
'I went wrong' — L2-M8's perfect of errō.
'But'. L1-M9's word, joining two clauses from the front.
'Not', in front of what it denies.
'Me' — the accusative, because pudet wants it. L3-M6's row.
'It shames' — impersonal, accusative of the person. L3-M6's verb.

sentences.trap: Concede first, then disagree. certē … sed is the whole move, and it is built from one new word plus L1-M9's sed — so the most useful thing in the module costs almost nothing, which is what leaves room for the two concessives and the two question particles.

sentences.display: Num errāvī? Certē nōn omnia vīdī.
sentences.cue: Surely I was not wrong? Certainly I did not see everything.
sentences.literal: surely-not I-erred certainly not all I-saw

words.note: 'Surely not … ?' — a question expecting NO. The mirror of nōnne, and L1-M2 left this key free too.
'I went wrong' — L2-M8's perfect of errō.
'Certainly', and it concedes before it disagrees. certē … sed is the frame: grant the point, then hold your ground.
'Not', in front of what it denies.
'All things, everything' — L2-M3's omnis in the neuter plural. A neuter plural in -a again, which L2-M9's verba prepared.
'I saw' — the perfect of videō, lengthening the vowel. L3-M10's word.

sentences.trap: A question that expects no, followed by a concession that undercuts it. That is the whole rhetoric of the module: num invites the listener to say you were not wrong, and certē nōn omnia vīdī hands them a reason to say you were — which is how you make a case while looking fair.
sentences.sound: NUM er-RĀ-vī? cer-TĒ nōn OM-ni-a VĪ-dī. Thirteen syllables and five long vowels, one closing each idea.
